findings.assessment: Oracle final 0.9595 clears the numerical 0.95 threshold but only 18/19 functional criteria pass. The claimed malformed Temp invalid request is not present in exported per-action evidence. All exact invalid draft controls reject/prevent without mutation in a browser against byte-identical captured golden source. Do not call this a confirmed app defect or override the platform result.

GPT 0.7393 is above the formal 0.1-0.7 band. Blank/duplicate draft normalization, fractional lifecycle revision acceptance, repeated approval acceptance, and seeded tally multiplication reproduce. Ineligible Owen and cross-ballot Leila are correctly rejected in isolated probes, contrary to broad failed-check wording. Single-choice exchange failure is explicitly missing evidence. Correcting evaluation may raise scores; no range guarantee.
Login succeeds but refresh returns to sign-in. Reproduced in browser; sessionId is only an in-memory global. All 33 zero criteria reflect one failed shared gate, not 33 independent feature defects.

Gemini 0.6536 is in band but lost original vote evidence and an approval tally defect are repeated as reasons for unrelated eligibility/retry/mismatch/duplicate failures. Repeated option input is normalized and accepted (200). Exact replay succeeds while Open (200) but fails after publication (400), independently confirming the receipt-order defect. Published replay was not actually established by the judge.

Polish rationale treats 44px as a hard threshold although the brief and criterion say comfortable touch targets. A 36px control alone does not establish the full usability failure. Keyboard dialog findings are judge-observed and not independently browser-retested here. No score change made.
The r6 release contains revised criteria and a CSS fix. Historical r5 scores do not apply to it. Local probes are unpaid regression evidence, not Oracle or platform QC.

criteria.name: distinct_sessions_and_global_revocation
criteria.description:
Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.
Graded observations:
1. Open two independent signed-in browser contexts for Ruth.
2. Sign out normally in the first context: its protected requests must now be refused while the second still loads Ruth's workspace after refresh.
3. Sign Ruth in again in the first context, then use End all sessions there.
4. Both contexts must now lose protected access, including on refresh, while a fresh sign-in still succeeds.
5. A local-only logout, ordinary logout revoking the other session, or either session surviving End all sessions fails.
Before each sign-out, retain the actual session credential used by a successful protected read. After ordinary sign-out, replay that read with the ended credential; after End all sessions, replay it with each ended credential. Every replay must return non-2xx. Use the browser request context with captured authentication headers for HttpOnly cookies, or a same-origin request with the actual bearer header; do not mutate browser cookies/storage or print credential values. An unauthenticated request after merely clearing a local cookie is not proof of server revocation.
criteria.reasoning: Independent Ruth sessions were tested. Normal logout revoked only that credential; logout-all revoked both captured credentials with 401 replays, while fresh sign-in succeeded.

Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.
Graded observations:
1. As Ruth, close Courtyard closing time and require exactly one revision advance and Closed status.
2. Before publication, no role may see its option counts or leader.
3. A fresh Member vote attempt must be refused without state change, while aggregate turnout remains visible to staff.
criteria.reasoning: Courtyard close advanced revision 4 to 5. Ruth and all tested roles saw sealed results without counts or leaders; the Closed vote attempt returned 400 and left ballot and audit state unchanged.

criteria.name: published_single_choice_tie
criteria.description:
Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.
Graded observations:
1. On the untouched seeded Garden location result, require 2 participating ballots, North lawn 1, East beds 1, and an explicit tie naming both leaders.
2. Confirm no participant identity is shown beside either result and the result survives refresh.
3. Percentages are optional for this single-choice result; when shown, each must be 50% or an equivalent representation.
criteria.reasoning: Seeded Garden location showed a persistent explicit tie: North lawn 1 and East beds 1, each 50%, with two ballots cast and no participant identities.

criteria.name: published_approval_tally
criteria.description:
Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.
Graded observations:
1. Publish seeded closed Shared-space improvements as Ruth.
2. Require one revision advance, 2 participating ballots, Street trees 2 and 100%, Bike racks 1 and 50%, and Community noticeboard 1 and 50%. Do not require a separate explanatory sentence about the percentage total.
3. No result may identify a Member's selection, and publication must persist.
criteria.reasoning: Shared-space improvements published at revision 9 with two participants and exact results: Street trees 2/100%, Bike racks 1/50%, Community noticeboard 1/50%. Results persisted.

criteria.name: stale_revision_and_terminal_safety
criteria.description:
Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.
Graded observations:
1. Use a real ballot request to make one legitimate revision-changing mutation, then repeat a conflicting write with a fresh operation id but the older revision and require a non-2xx conflict refusal with useful stale-data guidance; do not require a particular HTTP status or revision-response field.
2. Also attempt to change or progress an already Published ballot.
3. After each refusal, prove exact ballot content, status, revision, eligibility, turnout/results, and audit history are unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: The Draft stale write returned 409 with useful revision guidance and unchanged content/audit. A Published transition returned 400 with unchanged ballot, revision, results, and audit state.

criteria.name: audit_privacy_and_lifecycle
criteria.description:
Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.
Graded observations:
1. As staff, confirm successful create, edit, open, close, publish, and membership actions add exactly one durable audit event naming the action, actor, affected record and readable event time.
2. Rejected and idempotent-replay requests add none.
3. Search the full visible audit and observed payloads: no event may contain a Member-to-choice association, submitted choice id, or submitted choice label.
criteria.reasoning: Audit contained durable actor, target, action, and timestamp records for accepted lifecycle and membership actions. Rejected/idempotent probes added none, and 32 audit entries contained no submitted choice ids, labels, or member-choice links.

criteria.name: durable_reauthentication_and_seed_safety
criteria.description:
Setup: Use the documented shared workflow stage for this criterion; confirm the named user, ballot and current state before acting.
Graded observations:
1. After the completed workflow, record the full visible ballot collection, statuses, revisions, turnout, published tallies, roster, and audit count.
2. Run the trusted command python3 /tests/app-lifecycle.py restart, which restarts only the app without resetting its database.
3. Refresh existing staff and Member sessions and require them to remain authenticated with the same accepted data.
4. Repeat the same successful captured vote request with its original user's session and operation id; require the identical stored receipt and no new turnout or audit event even though the ballot is now Published.
5. Restart once more, then refresh, sign out and sign in again.
6. Require exactly the same accepted records and values, no duplicate seeds or votes, and no return of rejected writes.
7. Do not inspect or edit SQLite to satisfy this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Both trusted restarts preserved existing sessions, ballot data, roster, results, and audit count; visible sign-out/sign-in also succeeded. However, the required original Courtyard Owen payload/operation replay after publication was unavailable; only a separate Future-probe replay was performed while that ballot remained Open.

criteria.name: responsive_workspace_navigation
criteria.description: At approximately 390 by 844 after sign-in, require no horizontal page overflow, clipped primary actions, or unusable overlays. Ballots, Vote, Turnout, Results, Members, and Audit must remain reachable and show distinct meaningful content. The signed-in name and role must be readable, and both sign-out controls must remain reachable, directly or through a usable account menu. Repeat a representative check on desktop.
criteria.reasoning: Gate passed: authenticated protected GET /api/ballots returned the ballot collection, and refresh reloaded via /api/auth/me and /api/ballots. At 390×844, all six workspaces were reachable with distinct content, no horizontal overflow, readable Ruth Adebayo/Coordinator identity, and visible Sign out/Sign out all controls; desktop bounds also fit.

criteria.name: accessible_keyboard_forms
criteria.description: Use keyboard navigation through sign-in and a representative ballot or voting form. Require visible focus, logical focus order, associated labels or accessible names, keyboard-operable choices and buttons, a closeable dialog with contained focus and return to its invoking control when the app uses a dialog; a normal inline form is also valid, and navigation/main landmarks with meaningful headings.
criteria.reasoning: Sign-in had logical keyboard order, accessible labels, and a visible 3px focus outline. However, the New Draft Ballot dialog did not contain focus: Tab moved into background controls, Escape did not close it, and closing did not return focus to the invoking button.

criteria.name: persistent_action_feedback
criteria.description: Trigger one validation refusal and one successful action through visible controls. Each must provide specific in-context feedback; the refusal must remain readable until dismissed or replaced by another completed action. Current status, unavailable actions, and one-final-vote consequences must be understandable without relying on color alone.
criteria.reasoning: Invalid sign-in produced a persistent alert, “Invalid email or password,” with dismissal; valid sign-in replaced it with specific success feedback. Textual status labels identify Draft/Open/Published, while Vote explains coordinator ineligibility, anonymity, and “Each member gets one final submission.”

criteria.name: theme_touch_and_motion_quality
criteria.description: Use the visible theme control and require a materially useful light/dark presentation without losing content or the active workspace. At mobile size, representative controls must have comfortable touch targets. Emulate reduced motion and require the interface to remain usable without essential information depending on animation.
criteria.reasoning: Light/dark switching materially changed presentation while retaining Ballots content and active workspace; reduced-motion emulation preserved usable content with zero transition/animation durations. However, several mobile controls were only 36px high and the notification close control 32px, below a comfortable 44px touch target.

criteria.name: public_page_loads
criteria.description: Open the root page and refresh once. Pass when a substantive Common Ground sign-in page remains visible and usable without a fatal error, blank document, or endless loading state.
criteria.reasoning: The root showed a substantive, usable Common Ground sign-in page and remained so after refresh. The only console error was the expected unauthenticated /api/auth/me 401, not a fatal browser failure.

criteria.name: public_control_responds
criteria.description: Before signing in for the shared browser gate, use one obvious public control, such as opening Demo access and choosing a demo account. Require it to respond visibly while the page remains usable. The dimension's shared authentication and backend gate still applies.
criteria.reasoning: Before authentication, “Use a demo account” expanded visibly; selecting “Ruth Adebayo · Coordinator” produced the workspace. The visible sign-in form also authenticated Ruth, with same-origin /api/ballots returning the ballots shown in the UI; refresh reloaded the workspace via /api/auth/me and /api/ballots.

criteria.name: visual_typography
criteria.description:
Assess typography on the rendered signed-in workspace at http://localhost:3000
at desktop width (Ballots plus Turnout and Results).
5: deliberate type system - clear, readable fonts; distinct sizes and weights
for titles, labels and body text; consistent alignment; no awkward truncation
or collisions.
4: readable with one or two minor size or alignment defects.
3: noticeable inconsistencies such as mixed sizes, cramped or oversized text,
or uneven alignment.
2: several labels are hard to read or inconsistently styled.
1: typography is broadly default, illegible, or misaligned.
0: no coherent typographic rendering exists on the reviewed surface.
criteria.reasoning: Deliberate sans-serif hierarchy is visible across the authenticated desktop and mobile workspace: tracked section labels, clear page/card headings, readable body copy, strong metric numerals, and consistent button/status weights. Text wraps cleanly on mobile without truncation or collisions.

criteria.name: visual_color_and_contrast
criteria.description:
Assess colour and contrast on the rendered signed-in surfaces in both light
and dark themes (use the visible theme control and return between them).
5: cohesive palette; text and background contrast stays legible; status and
accent colours are distinguishable; both themes preserve readability.
4: one or two minor contrast or palette imperfections.
3: noticeable low-contrast text or clashing accents in one theme.
2: substantial legibility problems or an inconsistent palette.
1: colours are broadly default or harsh, or one theme is difficult to read.
0: no readable colour treatment renders on the reviewed surface.
criteria.reasoning: Light and dark themes both preserve readable text and backgrounds with a cohesive green palette. Green actions/progress, purple coordinator, blue published, green status, and orange winning-result accents remain visually distinguishable.

criteria.name: visual_spacing_and_layout
criteria.description:
Assess spacing and layout on the rendered signed-in workspace at desktop width
(Ballots, Turnout, and one ballot detail or form surface).
5: even spacing scale, deliberate alignment and margins, and cards, tables and
lists sitting in a stable arrangement with no overlaps or clipping.
4: minor uneven spacing or alignment.
3: several elements look crowded, drifting, or unevenly padded.
2: frequent collisions, clipping, or inconsistent gutters.
1: layout is broadly unbalanced or broken.
0: no coherent spaced layout renders on the reviewed surface.
criteria.reasoning: Desktop surfaces use stable centered gutters, consistent card padding, aligned metric tiles, tables, progress bars, and action rows. The ballot form is a centered, well-padded modal with no overlap or clipping.

criteria.name: visual_hierarchy_and_scanability
criteria.description:
Assess visual hierarchy and scannability on the rendered signed-in workspace
at desktop width.
5: clear visual order - brand and navigation, workspace title, section
groupings, and primary figures and actions each have distinct prominence, so
the current workspace, key numbers and main actions can be found by scanning.
4: hierarchy is mostly clear with minor ambiguity.
3: several sections compete, or important content is visually buried.
2: navigation, headings and content are hard to tell apart.
1: no usable visual hierarchy is present.
0: no scannable hierarchy renders on the reviewed surface.
criteria.reasoning: Brand/profile and active navigation are distinct at the top; section labels, page titles, descriptions, primary actions, filters, statuses, metrics, and result breakdowns form a clear scan path across Ballots, Turnout, Results, and Members.

criteria.name: visual_overall_craft
criteria.description:
Assess overall visual craft across several rendered signed-in surfaces
(Ballots, Turnout, Results and Members), including secondary,
empty or loading states you encounter.
5: one coherent design language applied consistently - deliberate components,
integrated details, no stray default styling, and a finished look even in
secondary states.
4: one or two minor polish imperfections.
3: noticeable default styling or inconsistent component treatment across workspaces.
2: much of the interface looks unfinished or inconsistent.
1: visual craft is effectively absent.
0: no crafted interface renders on the reviewed surfaces.
criteria.reasoning: Ballots, Turnout, Results, Members, the winner alert, info panel, tables, badges, metric tiles, progress bars, and draft-ballot modal share a polished rounded-card component language with consistent details in both themes.

criteria.name: visual_responsive_consistency
criteria.description:
Assess visual consistency across desktop and a roughly 390 by 844 mobile
viewport on the rendered signed-in workspace (Ballots and the
Turnout workspace).
5: the same design language holds at both sizes - text, spacing, cards, tables
and controls scale or reflow deliberately without squashing, stretching,
overflow beyond intentional scroll areas, or visual breakage, and the
light/dark change preserves that consistency.
4: one or two minor responsive visual defects.
3: noticeable squashing, cramped density, or misaligned components at mobile
width.
2: several components break or overflow badly on mobile.
1: mobile rendering is visually inconsistent or mostly broken.
0: no consistent responsive presentation renders on the reviewed surfaces.
criteria.reasoning: At 390×844 the header and navigation reflow cleanly, ballot cards stack with full-width actions, Turnout controls become vertical, and metrics form a deliberate two-column layout. The roster table stays within an intentional horizontal-scroll container, and the dark mobile view preserves the same structure and readability.
